title: Elastic priority tiers and cross-region spillover admission controller
creator: Asha Raman
description: Design and implement an admission controller that combines elastic priority tiers with cross-region spillover to enforce SLOs under extreme load. Must support per-tenant priorities, dynamic demotion/promotion based on recent SLO burn, and graceful degradation modes (cache-first, context trimming, quantized-model fallback, canned stubs).
background: We currently have static priority lanes and simple rate limits. Incidents in the last two quarters showed that static lanes either exhaust capacity or cause blast radius for noisy tenants. Multi-region failover amplifies the problem when primary region saturates: we see queue buildup + retry storms in the failing region and suboptimal routing to secondary regions without coordinated shedding. This ticket captures a new admission strategy to reduce p99 latency spikes and control error-budget burn while preserving high-value traffic.
proposal: Introduce an Elastic Priority Tier (EPT) controller with the following properties: 1) time-decayed credit buckets per tenant and per-route, 2) latency-aware admission that factors p99 vs. median degradation, 3) automatic fragile-tenants demotion to best-effort lanes after sustained SLO breaches, 4) controlled spillover to remote regions with capacity-aware admission to avoid creating remote hotspots, and 5) graceful degradation modes that route admitted requests through cheaper/low-latency fallbacks when necessary.
implementation_steps: Instrument per-tenant and per-route token counters and recent SLO burn rate (30m/1h windows)
Implement EPT admission module in runtime: credit buckets + admission scoring function (priority_weight, credit_balance, predicted_latency_penalty)
Add region-aware spillover policy: evaluate remote region headroom via runtime health API before rerouting; attach spillover weight to requests
Create demotion controller: if tenant error budget burn > threshold for X minutes then move tenant to lower tier and notify billing/SEs
Add graceful degradation hooks: cache-prefetch, context-trimming policy, quantized-model fallback (quant-8), canned-stub responses for ultra-low-priority classes
Expose observability: per-tenant shedding rate, queue histograms, spillover counts, demotion events, and SLO burn dashboards
End-to-end tests + chaos experiments (region failover + load generator)
rollout_plan: Canary in hosted region us-east-1 with 10% of traffic (low-risk tenants), monitor burn-rate and p99. If stable for 48h, expand to 50% and enable cross-region spillover for non-critical routes. Final global rollout gated on two successful chaos runs and runbook signoff.
metrics: shedding rate (requests rejected or downgraded) by tenant and route
spillover requests per minute and spillover success ratio
retry amplification factor after shedding events
demotion count and time-to-recovery per tenant
testing_plan: Unit tests for admission scoring and credit decay logic
Integration tests with runtime routing and fallback paths (quantized model, cache)
Chaos tests: kill primary region replicas while generating mixed-priority traffic
Load tests: ramp noisy-tenant traffic and validate p99 containment and shedding rates
Simulated billing/notification flows for demoted tenants
risks: Retry storms: aggressive shedding without client-side backoff could shift load to other regions
Thundering fallbacks: switching many requests to quantized fallback simultaneously may overload fallback endpoints
Incorrect demotion criteria causing customer surprise/SE escalations
Observability blind spots will make tuning hard if per-tenant metrics are sparse
Latency bias: admission scoring must avoid over-prioritizing median latency at expense of tail experienced by critical tenants
